text: dsh-file-drag 是适用于 DSH Web 客户端的文件拖放插件。它在右侧 Files 侧栏文件或文件夹行上启用拖动，并接收拖放到编辑器的项目。用户可将项目插入为编辑器原生引用卡片、作为附件上传，或插入相对路径形式的 @ 提及；设置页可选择默认方式，按住 Alt 可单次改用路径提及。附件模式通过 workspaceFiles 读取文件字节，再交给编辑器处理。代码未定义 API 密钥或外部服务配置。

dsh-file-drag lets DSH web users drag files and folders from the Files sidebar into the composer as reference chips, uploaded attachments, or relative-path @ mentions. Choose the default in General Settings; hold Alt for a one-time @ mention. Attachment mode reads bytes through workspaceFiles.
想把右侧 Files 里的文件直接拖进正在写的消息。
DSH 能把工作区文件插入成可选择的引用卡片吗？
我想把侧栏文件作为附件或 @ 路径放进编辑器。
dsh-file-drag 的功能「拖放文件到编辑器」：在 Files 侧栏拖动文件或文件夹到编辑器，可按当前模式插入原生引用卡片、附件或相对路径 @ 提及；目录不走附件上传。
dsh-file-drag 的功能「选择放置方式」：General Settings 中可选择内嵌卡片、附件或 @ 路径作为默认结果；拖放时按住 Alt 可临时插入 @ 路径。

dsh-file-drag README · dsh-file-drag：Drag files and folders from the DeepSeek Harness **Files** sidebar straight into the message composer. By default each dropped file becomes a small inline chip inside the sentence you are writing — the same rounded token the composer's own `@` picker produces — and you can switch that to an uploaded attachment or a plain `@` path.

dsh-file-drag README · dsh-file-drag：DeepSeek Harness already accepts file drags that come from the operating system, but its Sidebar Files pane has no drag source at all, and the composer only claims drags whose payload type is `Files`. This plugin closes that gap from the outside: it arms the existing file rows, carries the relative path over a private MIME type, and then hands the result to the composer through its own insertion paths.

dsh-file-drag README · Do you need this?：Watch the clip above before installing anything. The plugin only changes one thing:
it lets a file in the right-hand **Files** tab become something you can drop into
the middle of a sentence.

- You keep material in the workspace and refer to it by path while writing → you
  will use this every day.
- You paste code inline, or never open the Files tab → skip it. Nothing else in the
  app changes, and there is nothing to configure.
dsh-file-drag README · Do you need this?：**Repository and releases:** <https://github.com/JiayuREN1127/dsh-file-drag>

dsh-file-drag README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** or a build that still renders the right sidebar Files tab.
- The `desktop` profile (`~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`), which is what the macOS app uses.

dsh-file-drag README · Install：```bash
git clone https://github.com/JiayuREN1127/dsh-file-drag.git
cd dsh-file-drag
./install.sh
```

dsh-file-drag README · From a market index：The repository also publishes a format-1 market index. Add this URL under
**Settings → Plugins → Discover → Index sources** to install and update the plugin
from there:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JiayuREN1127/dsh-file-drag/main/market/index.json
```

`install.sh` copies the package into `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-file-drag` and appends one Loader row to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`, keeping a timestamped backup of that file first.

dsh-file-drag README · From a market index：To install by hand, do the same two things:

1. Copy this package to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-file-drag`.
2. Append to `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: file-drag
      name: dsh-file-drag
```

Then **quit the app completely (`Cmd-Q`) and reopen it**. The Loader tree is built at startup, so a page reload is not enough for the first install. Later plugin updates only need a page reload.

dsh-file-drag README · Usage：1. Open the **Files** tab in the right sidebar.
2. Press and drag a file or a folder onto the message composer.
3. Release.

While dragging, the composer shows a dashed outline so you know it will accept the drop.

dsh-file-drag README · Drop behaviour：Pick it in **Settings → General → File drag**:

| Mode | Result |
|---|---|
| **Inline chip** (default) | A small rounded card with the file icon and name lands in the sentence, exactly where the caret is. It is the composer's own reference token, so it moves, wraps and deletes like text. |
| **Attachment** | The file is read and uploaded, and appears in the attachment rail above the composer. |
| **@ path** | The relative path is inserted as plain text, e.g. `@src/client/index.ts`. |

dsh-file-drag README · Drop behaviour：Hold **Alt (⌥)** while dropping to get the plain `@` path once, without changing the setting.

The preference is stored per client under the `dsh-file-drag:mode` key in `localStorage`.

dsh-file-drag README · Drop behaviour：| Source row | Inline chip | Attachment | @ path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/client/index.ts` | chip labelled `index.ts` | uploaded card | `@src/client/index.ts ` |
| folder `packages` | chip labelled `packages/` | falls back to a chip | `@packages/ ` |
| `my notes.md` | chip labelled `my notes.md` | uploaded card | `@"my notes.md" ` |

dsh-file-drag README · Drop behaviour：Paths keep the composer's own `formatFileMention` grammar: folders end with a slash and whitespace is quoted. A chip that cannot be placed falls back to the `@` path form, so a drop is never silently lost.

dsh-file-drag README · How it works：**Drag source.** The Files tab renders every row as `<li data-files-entry="file|directory|other" data-files-path="relative/path">`. The plugin does not guess the tree shape: on `pointerdown` it sets `draggable` on the closest such row, so the press can turn into a drag.

dsh-file-drag README · How it works：**Transport.** `dragstart` writes a private payload, `application/x-dsh-file-path`, holding the relative path and the entry kind. The native `Files` type is deliberately not used for the drag itself, because a synthesized `File` has no host path and the desktop path bridge would reject it.

dsh-file-drag README · How it works：**Inline chip.** On drop the plugin reaches the resident composer shell for the session and calls its `addFiles` with one reference — the same call the composer makes when you pick a file from the `@` menu — so the full Lexical decorator node, icon, label and clipboard projection all come from DeepSeek Harness itself. The session-scoped `conversation` service is reached through `ctx.sessions.binding(id).ctx.get("conversation")`, because a root-level plugin cannot inject a session-scoped service.

dsh-file-drag README · How it works：**Attachment.** The plugin reads the file through the `workspaceFiles` client Remote (`readBytes`), wraps the bytes in a real `File`, and replays the built-in `Files` drop onto the composer. The composer then takes its own upload path, so the card behaves exactly like one dragged in from the operating system.

dsh-file-drag README · How it works：**@ path.** The mention is delivered as a synthetic `paste` event carrying `text/plain` on the editor root. The draft editor is Lexical, which ignores direct DOM writes and `document.execCommand`; a paste is the only reliable way in.

**Settings row.** The preference is a row registered into the `settings.general.item` slot, so it appears in DeepSeek Harness's own Settings page and follows the UI language.

dsh-file-drag README · Compatibility：Built against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2`. The plugin depends on implementation details that are not a public contract:

- the `data-files-entry` / `data-files-path` attributes on sidebar rows,
- the composer being a `[contenteditable="true"]` element that handles `paste`,
- the composer component carrying a `sessionId` prop,
- the `settings.general.item` settings slot and the `conversation` service face,
- `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` as the client bundle entry point.

dsh-file-drag README · Compatibility：If a future release changes any of these, the plugin degrades instead of breaking the page: every handler is guarded, a failed chip insertion falls back to the `@` path, and `apply` is wrapped so a failure never blocks boot.

dsh-file-drag README · Limitations：- One item per drag; multi-select dragging is not implemented.
- Only works while the Files tab is rendered, because the rows are the drag source.
- Drops are accepted anywhere in the window, not only over the composer.
- Attachment mode reads files through the workspace-files Remote, so it inherits that service's size limit; oversized files fall back to a chip.
- The mention is relative to the Files tab root, which is the session workspace. A session opened in another folder still receives the same relative path.

dsh-file-drag README · Uninstall：```bash
rm -rf ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-file-drag
cp ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml.bak-<timestamp> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml
```

Then restart the app.
